name: Sustainability
answer: These measures show the carbon, water and energy sourcing behind a data center's operation. AI demand has made data centers one of the fastest growing users of electricity, so these figures are where climate commitments meet actual consumption.

metrics.line: Liters of water consumed by the facility, chiefly for evaporative cooling, per kilowatt-hour of IT energy delivered.
metrics.label: WUE, Water Usage Effectiveness

metrics.line: Kilograms of carbon dioxide emitted, from the grid mix and on-site generation, per kilowatt-hour of IT energy.
metrics.label: CUE, Carbon Usage Effectiveness

metrics.line: The share of facility consumption matched by renewable generation, reported either as annual matching through purchased certificates or as around-the-clock hourly matching.
metrics.label: Renewable energy utilization

reading.body:
Data center sustainability is measured per kilowatt-hour of IT energy delivered, not per facility or per dollar. Water usage effectiveness reports liters consumed, chiefly for evaporative cooling. Carbon usage effectiveness reports kilograms of carbon dioxide from the grid mix and on-site generation. Renewable energy utilization reports the share of consumption matched by renewable generation.

The common denominator is the unit of useful compute, which is what makes these figures comparable across sites and over time. A facility can lower its water number by shifting to less evaporative cooling, but that choice usually raises electricity use, so the three measures have to be read together rather than one at a time. AI demand has made data centers one of the fastest growing users of electricity, which is why these ratios now carry weight beyond a sustainability report.

Renewable energy utilization is the softest of the three, because the data distinguishes two ways of counting. Annual matching through purchased certificates and around-the-clock hourly matching can produce very different numbers for the same facility. A high share under annual matching does not mean the servers ran on renewable power at the hours they ran.

The data does not give target values, thresholds, or how any operator currently performs. It defines the measures and nothing more. It also does not cover the embodied carbon of the buildings and hardware themselves, only the emissions from operating them.
